description: Solo participant. Developing an autonomous 'Greenhouse Bot' for the Lunar South Pole under the Lunar Landing Site Navigator challenge, focusing on automated plant cultivation and life support resource management
summary: For the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge (Lunar Landing Site Navigator), Team PROJECT 404 presents an advanced autonomous reconnaissance rover designed for Faustini Rim A at the Lunar South Pole. Our rover solves extreme lighting, cryogenic thermal survival, and communication constraints by combining a rocker-bogie chassis, deployable tri-fold solar wings, and a Plutonium-238 radioisotope power/thermal core. Utilizing pre-loaded NASA Moon Trek digital elevation matrices within its RAD750 flight computer and stereoscopic binocular cameras, the rover autonomously maps safe astronaut landing zones and detects subsurface water-ice. Collected regolith and volatile samples are safely preserved inside an onboard hermetic vault for future crew retrieval, ensuring a robust bridge between robotic exploration and sustainable lunar base establishment.
details: Project Overview & Objectives: Team PROJECT 404 developed an autonomous reconnaissance and greenhouse rover tailored for Faustini Rim A at the Moon's South Pole. The mission focuses on safe astronaut landing zone certification, surface hazard mapping, and subsurface water-ice prospecting. ​How It Works & Technology: ​Chassis & Mobility: A springless 6-wheel rocker-bogie chassis with cleated titanium wheels maintains continuous ground contact across extreme crater slopes and rugged terrain. ​Power & Thermal: A hybrid architecture combining deployable tri-fold solar wings (for sunlit ridges) and a Plutonium-238 radioisotope power/thermal core (for permanently shadowed regions - PSRs) ensures continuous survival against cryogenic thermal shock below -200°C. ​Navigation & Software: Utilizes pre-loaded NASA Moon Trek digital elevation matrices combined with a radiation-hardened RAD750 flight computer, stereoscopic binocular cameras, active LiDAR, and RIMFAX subsurface radar for autonomous SLAM localization and hazard avoidance. ​Science & Caching: An articulated multi-DOF sampling arm drills into icy regolith and stores core samples securely inside an onboard hermetic vault for future astronaut retrieval
